analysis:
Examined ProviderLoop.swift in the base units against the patch. The head changes are small: new actor state (lines 719-730) and one init assignment (line 882). The new state is `selectedModelRecovery`, `selectedModelRecoveryLoadOverride`, `savedEnabledModels` (seeded from `config.config.backend.enabledModels`) and `enabledModelsAtLastSwitch`. These are internal stored properties only, and the diff adds no logic.

The test override closure is internal and nil by default, so it adds no production attack surface. The diff adds no network, crypto, attestation, key, cache or file-I/O handling. Unchanged are the X25519 key generation, the signer creation, the coordinator-facing SendHandle and the prefix-cache plumbing (T-041, TB-007 and TB-002 context).

Security-relevant behavior lives in the companion files (ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery and the SelectedModelRecovery type), which are not supplied. Open integration questions for those files: (1) whether recovery loads re-check the advertised-set guard, weight-hash verification and memory admission as `ensureModelLoaded` does, so that T-027 and T-012 are not bypassed; (2) whether the recovery path respects the admission barriers (drain, update, add-on hold per T-059) and the autopilot/eviction rules; (3) whether `savedEnabledModels`, read from the config file by the policy refresh, can only narrow serving and never add unverified models. I identified no concrete regression in the supplied evidence.
